solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do for one bishop and cleric, looking back

indicators.note: something looking back faces the other way, so the string built so far is read from right to left

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric's title

explanation.surface: A bishop and a cleric arrange to stand in for someone, glancing over their shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: B plus REV gives BREV, which read backwards is VERB.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'do' is an example of a part of speech expressing action, so 'for one' marks it as a sample.

clue.text: Old evil upset speakers — they may go into further detail

definitions.text: they may go into further detail

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the word for old evil is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: bale is an archaic word for evil or woe
orators are public speakers

explanation.surface: Speakers distressed by some ancient wickedness keep adding more and more detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Bale in this sense survives today mainly in the adjective 'baleful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who elaborate expand a statement by supplying extra particulars, a cryptic description of people.

clue.text: Support given to female, one Socialist, worked out badly

blocks.note: to back is to support
F is the standard abbreviation for female
I is the Roman numeral one
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Backing a woman who is a socialist candidate ended up going wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that backfires produces the opposite of its intended result, an idiom from guns misfiring.

clue.text: Performer, one sensible about places like London, not half

indicators.note: not half means only one of the two halves survives, so the back half is dropped
about means going round, so the sensible person surrounds the shortened word

blocks.note: a realist is a sensible, practical person
London is an example of a city

explanation.surface: An entertainer, a level-headed type, only half takes to big urban centres like London.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is what gets halved: six letters down to three, not the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitalist gives solo musical or poetic recitals, so the person is a kind of performing artist.

clue.text: Food that is eagerly sought by numismatist?

definitions.note: describes the thing sought, a scarce coin

blocks.note: first meaning: a dish of melted cheese on toast
second meaning, split in two: a scarce coin wanted by a coin collector

explanation.surface: A coin collector hungrily hunts down a particular snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A numismatist collects coins; split the answer as RARE BIT and it is an uncommon coin, a bit being an old word for a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese sauce grilled on toast, a classic British savoury dish served as a light meal.

clue.text: Lack of concern shown briefly by Vicky and Priscilla

blocks.clueFragment: shown briefly by Vicky and Priscilla
blocks.note: surface reading: two women behave callously towards someone for a short while
setter's reading: the abbreviation for the temperature word sits at the very centre of both names, so each name has that letter as its heart

explanation.surface: Two women, Vicky and Priscilla, are momentarily callous towards someone.
explanation.walkthrough: C, short for cold, is the middle letter of VICKY and of PRISCILLA, so both names are literally C-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold-heartedness is unfeeling indifference to others' suffering, an absence of sympathy or warmth.

clue.text: Jolly lot with very big drink container?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a brand name used as a general term

blocks.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, so the lot of them is THE RM
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A cheerful crowd with an enormous drink to share.
explanation.walkthrough: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, and RM is that corps' abbreviation, so 'Jolly lot' reads as THE RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermos is a trademark vacuum flask that keeps beverages hot or cold, a brand used generically.

clue.text: That is the day for assassination, foremost of tragedies

indicators.note: foremost picks out only the leading letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: Caesar was killed on the Ides of March
the opening letter of tragedies

explanation.surface: A grim aside about the day of Caesar's murder, the start of tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin phrase abbreviated as i.e., meaning 'in other words' when clarifying something.

clue.text: Musical group turning up that may be in the groove

definitions.text: that may be in the groove

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A band arriving that plays right in the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the groove' sounds like musical slang, matching the band, but it is meant literally: carpentry, not jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is a projecting tongue of wood made to fit into a mortise or slot in a joint.

clue.text: Pub about to sway with English song

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
ca is short for circa, about
to roll is to sway from side to side
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Swaying in a pub during an English singalong.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarolle is a Venetian gondolier's boating tune, so it is a type of vocal piece.

clue.text: Veg, not quite enough for a feast

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a beano is British slang for a party or feast

explanation.surface: A complaint that the vegetables won't stretch to a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: Beano is informal British for a celebration or knees-up; dropping its last letter leaves the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad, runner and green varieties are all edible pods or seeds, common garden vegetables.

clue.text: Prisoner with fantastic chatter

blocks.note: a con is a convict
fab is short for fabulous

explanation.surface: A convict with a wonderful gift of the gab.
explanation.definitionFit: Confab is informal shortening of confabulation, an informal talk or gossip session.

clue.text: Scottish town hospital attended by a poet

blocks.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
taken as written
John Milton wrote Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A poet visits a hospital in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is a large town in South Lanarkshire, south-east of Glasgow.

clue.text: Legal opinions in old rambling diatribe enthralling court

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters stray into a new order
enthralling means holding captive, so the jumbled word holds the court abbreviation inside it

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the letters to be rearranged
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Judges' opinions buried in an antiquated tirade that captivates the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter dicta are a judge's incidental remarks in a judgment, Latin for things said in passing.

clue.text: Royal survivor giving what is expected to an audience

indicators.note: something delivered to an audience is heard rather than read

blocks.note: par is the expected standard, as in golf

explanation.surface: A royal who lived through it all gives the crowd the expected performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII's six wives are remembered by 'divorced, beheaded, died; divorced, beheaded, survived'.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr, Henry VIII's sixth wife, outlived the king, hence the queen who survived.

clue.text: Is part-time working offering a sense of togetherness?

indicators.note: working suggests something being worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question of whether part-time employment builds camaraderie among colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the feeling of loyalty and cooperation shared by members of a group.

clue.text: Popular army officer usually

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked commanding officer, as is typically the case.
explanation.definitionFit: In general is an idiom meaning as a rule, for the most part, or on the whole.

clue.text: Oliver’s college?

blocks.note: surface reading: the college some man named Oliver attended
setter's reading: Oliver is the eighteenth-century Irish writer of She Stoops to Conquer, whose surname with a possessive names a London college

explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmiths is a college of the University of London; Oliver Goldsmith wrote The Vicar of Wakefield, so the college looks like it is his.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmiths, University of London, is an arts-focused institution in New Cross named after a livery company.

clue.text: Bloke holding drunk up is a sugary type

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for drunk is read bottom to top
holding means gripping something inside, so the bloke surrounds the other word

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A man propping up his drunken friend is a sweet sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugary type' reads as a sweet-natured person, but it means a kind of sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Maltose is malt sugar, a disaccharide formed when starch breaks down, so it is a sugar variety.

clue.text: Scorn during school tests — they inflict unnecessary pain

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the word for scorn goes inside the tests

blocks.note: dis is slang for disrespect or scorn
SATs are standardised tests in schools

explanation.surface: Pupils who mock others during exams are cruel tormentors.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadists take pleasure in causing suffering to others, named after the Marquis de Sade.

clue.text: Member turning to entertain a Highlander?

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the word for member is read backwards
to entertain is to host someone, so the turned word takes the letter in

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, or member
taken as written

explanation.surface: A club member changes course to host a visitor from the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Celt, typically associated with the Scottish Highlands; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Fool was unwell, being attacked

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
ailed means was sick

explanation.surface: An idiot who was ill was then set upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being attacked' matches the participle: 'he was assailed' and 'he was being attacked' swap cleanly in passive use.
explanation.definitionFit: Assailed is the past tense of assail, to attack violently or verbally.

clue.text: Cold? It’s good to wear a hat

indicators.note: to wear a hat is to have it on top, so the letter for good sits inside the hat phrase

blocks.note: a lid is slang for a hat
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Advice that on a chilly day it is wise to put on a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Algid is a rare medical and literary word meaning chilly or icy, from Latin algidus.

clue.text: Sarah is turning up as apostle’s companion

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the words are read upwards, back to front

blocks.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sarah shows up as the travelling partner of one of Christ's followers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Acts, Silas accompanied the apostle Paul on his second missionary journey.

clue.text: Strip joint vulgar, first to go

indicators.note: first to go means the opening letter leaves the word for vulgar

blocks.note: a den is a dive or low joint
rude means vulgar

explanation.surface: A seedy strip club, crude, where the first act goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip joint' reads as one phrase, but 'Strip' is the definition and 'joint' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to lay bare, removing a covering, so it works as a verb meaning to make naked.

clue.text: Diary about daughter is something precious

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for diary faces the other way

blocks.note: a log is a daily record
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A treasured diary about one's daughter is a valuable keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is the classic valuable metal, prized in jewellery and as wealth.

clue.text: Excessively severe maidens possibly conned, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase must be spoken out and judged by its sound

blocks.note: maidens are cricket overs bowled without a run scored, and conned means fooled

explanation.surface: Young women perhaps duped by an overly harsh guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a maiden is one where no runs come, so maidens are examples of overs.
explanation.definitionFit: Overstrict means too rigid or stern in discipline, adding 'over' to signal excess.

clue.text: Annoys sides playing with interrupting requests

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are in action, moving about freely
something interrupting comes in the middle, breaking up the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
pleas are appeals

explanation.surface: Teams on the field get irritated when their game is broken up by appeals.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease is to irritate or upset someone, a close synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Report of solitary advance

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word is judged by sound alone

blocks.note: lone means solitary

explanation.surface: News of a single step forward.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is money handed over before it is due, to be repaid, which is a kind of borrowing.
